items.description: A historic fortress built by the Spanish in 1737 to defend their borders in the Chuy region. It is now a museum displaying colonial artifacts and military history.
The 18th-century home of Juan Antonio Lavalleja, a key figure in the Uruguayan independence movement. Today it serves as a museum preserving personal belongings and historical documents.
A neoclassical palace in Montevideo that served as the official seat of the Uruguayan government for many years. It now houses a museum dedicated to the country's presidential history.
An iconic football stadium built for the inaugural 1930 FIFA World Cup. It remains the home stadium for the Uruguayan national team and a historic monument of world football.
The most important performing arts theater in Uruguay, inaugurated in 1856. It is renowned for its neoclassical architecture and rich cultural programming.
The tallest building in Uruguay, standing 158 meters high. This modern glass tower is a landmark of contemporary architecture in the Montevideo bay area.
A historic lighthouse located in a remote coastal village with no electricity. It has guided ships through the treacherous Atlantic waters since 1881.
A peculiar castle built in the early 20th century by Francisco Piria, the founder of Piriápolis. It blends European styles and is filled with alchemical symbols.
A masterpiece of modernist architecture designed by Eladio Dieste using reinforced brick. It is internationally recognized for its innovative undulating shapes.
A famous bronze monument in Parque Batlle depicting ox-drawn carts used by early settlers. It is a tribute to the pioneers of the Uruguayan nation.
